subject: Residency & Retention API contract proposal
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice@finco.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Residency & retention API contract proposal

Hi Alice,

Thanks again for walking through FinCo's compliance needs this week. As promised, attached is a first-pass proposal for a tenant-scoped Residency & Retention API that would give you programmatic control over:

- storage_residency: region code(s) where persistent assets are stored (e.g. us-west-2, eu-west-1)
- retention_ttl_days: per-tenant default TTL applied to generated data
- deletion_policy: {"soft_delete" | "hard_delete" | "legal_hold"} and optional retention_exempt_paths
- migration_mode: {"live-migrate" | "redirect-writes"} and migration_window estimate hooks

Key guarantees we propose:
- REST API for policy management and an events-based async migration for cross-region moves
- Audit log entries (WORM) for every policy change and deletion request
- Proof-of-deletion artifact (signed timestamped log) available after hard-delete runs

I attached two artifacts: a YAML sketch of the API surface (residency-api-draft.yaml) and a high-level Data Deletion Playbook (data-deletion-playbook.pdf). We're not locking anything down yet — looking for your must-haves and any constraints from your compliance/legal teams.

Questions for you:
1) Is per-tenant TTL sufficient, or do you need per-resource-type TTLs (embeddings vs. logs vs. docs)?
2) Do you require immediate hard-delete on request, or is an N-day window acceptable for operational sanity?
3) Are there any regional data sovereignty specifics for particular product lines we should know about?

If it helps, happy to sync with your security and procurement folks next week. Proposed times: Tue/Wed 10–12 PT.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai
(650) 555-0142

Attachments: residency-api-draft.yaml (text), data-deletion-playbook.pdf (pdf)
From: Alice Chen <alice@finco.com>

Cc: security@finco.com, procurement@finco.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:08:23 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency & retention API contract proposal

Rachel — thanks for the detailed starter. A few items from our side after an initial pass:

1) Proof-of-deletion: We need a cryptographically verifiable artifact that shows the objects were removed and a signed audit trail for at least 3 years. Can you point to how Redwood will generate and retain that artifact?
2) Migration windows: For business continuity, FinCo requires zero-downtime reads during region migration. We prefer the model where writes go to the new region while reads are served from the old region until migration completes. What's your expected window for a 1TB tenant?
3) KMS + key rotation: We use a customer-managed key in AWS KMS. Any migration must preserve encryption semantics and allow rekeying without data expiry.
4) SLA/contract language: procurement wants a clause tying residence guarantees to credits if data is stored outside declared regions.

Also tagging our security lead (security@finco.com) and procurement. We'd like a short call to align on the proof-of-deletion and SLA language — Thu or Mon morning PT works for us.

Thanks,
Alice Chen
Head of Cloud Compliance, FinCo Financial
alice@finco.com

Copying in Monica and Priyom. Good questions from FinCo — here's a rough technical response and ask for engineering estimates: 

- Proof-of-deletion: We can produce signed deletion manifests generated by the control plane at the end of hard-delete jobs. The manifest will include object identifiers, job id, timestamp, and a SHA256 of the manifest signed by the platform HSM key. We should confirm FinCo's acceptance criteria for "cryptographically verifiable."

- Migration approach: We support two modes: 1) redirect-writes (quick) where new writes are pinned to the target region; 2) live-migrate where we stream+apply data to target and verify checksums. For 1TB I'd estimate a migration window dependent on BW — rough ballpark 2–8 hours if using bulk snapshot + parallel apply, longer for many small objects. Priyom, engineering input?

- KMS: We can integrate customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS) and perform envelope rewrapping during migration. Need to scope whether rewrapping is synchronous (adds latency) or async (background job).

Action items:
- Monica: define SLOs and fallback behavior for reads during migration (soft-read-fallback TTLs etc.).
- Priyom: quick engineering estimate for live-migrate throughput per GPU node and for metadata-heavy tenants.
- Rachel: get FinCo to confirm per-resource TTL requirement.

I'll draft an engineering-friendly contract appendix that captures manifest format, retention granularity, and allowed migration modes.

—Marcus
Product Manager, Platform
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Quick reliability notes and rollout plan: 

1) Rollout strategy: feature-flag the API, enable for a small set of dedicated customers first, then canary across Dedicated clusters before turning on in Hosted. Provide a console toggle and an SDK helper to atomically update policy plus a migration job trigger.

2) Telemetry: emit metrics for migration progress (bytes migrated, objects verified), policy-change events, failed deletion attempts, and proof-of-deletion issuance. We'll need alerting thresholds and an SLO for deletion job success rate.

3) Runbook: I've attached a short runbook stub (migration-runbook.md). It includes rollback steps and a verification checklist (checksum verification, sampling, and FIPS key handling notes). Security review required before canary.

4) Timeline ask: if engineering can provide estimates by EOD Wed we'll propose a concrete timeline to FinCo.

Monica Patel
Head of Reliability Engineering, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
